record.original_question: Does ρ has other discontinuity? What are they? Is ρ piece-wise constant?

evidence.quote: Does ρ has other discontinuity? What are they? Is ρ piece-wise constant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number α > 1 and a finite word w over the alphabet {0,1}, say that w contains an α-power if there exist a nonempty word x and a prefix y of x such that w has a factor equal to x^k y (for some integer k ≥ 1) with (k|x| + |y|)/|x| = α. A binary word is α-power-free if it contains no β-power with β ≥ α (in the standard "≥-power-free" convention used for fractional exponents). Let L_α ⊆ {0,1}* denote the language of all finite α-power-free binary words, and let s_α(n) = |L_α ∩ {0,1}^n|. Define the binary power-free growth function

  ρ(α) = lim sup_{n → ∞} s_α(n)^{1/n},   for α > 1.

It is known that ρ is non-decreasing, that ρ(α) = 0 for α ≤ 2 (apart from finitely many words there are no binary square-free words), and that ρ is discontinuous at α = 2 (the value jumps to a positive number for α slightly greater than 2). 

(a) Determine whether ρ has any discontinuities other than the one at α = 2, and if so locate and describe all such points of discontinuity.

(b) Determine whether the function ρ : (1, ∞) → [0, 2] is piecewise constant, i.e. whether there exists a (possibly infinite) partition of (1, ∞) into intervals on each of which ρ is constant.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up related work by Shur and others on growth rates of power-free languages, including a 2025 proof of Shur's large-alphabet conjecture and recent work on low-complexity binary words avoiding (5/2)+-powers, but no source explicitly resolves whether the binary power-free growth function ρ has discontinuities other than at α = 2 or whether it is piecewise constant. The status appears unresolved in publicly available literature.

status_evidence.title: A Proof of Shur's Conjecture on the Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Shur conjectured estimates for exponential growth rates of (n/(n-1))-free and (n/(n-1))+-free languages over k-letter alphabets; settled for large k.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress concerns growth rates over large alphabets, not the structure of ρ on the binary alphabet.

status_evidence.title: Low complexity binary words avoiding (5/2)+-powers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies binary words avoiding (5/2)+-powers and their factor complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work refines understanding of specific binary power-free thresholds but does not characterize all discontinuities of ρ.

status_evidence.title: Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the function whose values are exponential growth rates of β-power-free languages over k-letter alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: General properties of growth rate functions are studied, but discontinuity structure on the binary alphabet remains open.
